title: Stand a pile of flat-lying books upright on a shelf in alphabetical order of their spine codes
instruction: Stand the four books upright on the shelf with their spines facing out, in alphabetical order of the four-letter codes on their spines, from left to right.
context: Putting books back on a shelf in order is familiar from homes, classrooms and libraries, and returned books arrive in a pile, lying flat. A hand coming straight down on the pile can lift a book but cannot stand it up. Each book has to be pinched by the 14 mm of spine edge that sticks out past the book beneath, lifted clear without dragging the next one off the pile, turned upright by a quarter turn of the wrist, slid into its place, often between two books already standing, and pushed home. The pile's order is unrelated to the codes, and two codes in each layout share their first letters, so each book's place has to be read from its spine. Unlike shelving tasks that start with books already standing and accept any order, the books here start flat and each has one correct place.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Layout A is given first, layout B in brackets. Books: four pocket-format paperbacks, each 80 mm deep (spine to fore-edge), 120 mm tall and 26 mm thick, 160 g, with covers in red, green, blue and ochre from the top of the pile down. Each has a cream label down its spine with a four-letter code in black block capitals 21 mm tall and 15 mm wide, reading from head to tail. Pile: the four books lie flat, face up, one on another, on a fixed dark grey stand 4.5 cm tall, 6.6 cm deep and 10 cm wide. Their spines face the arms and their heads point left. Each book lies 14 mm nearer the arms than the one beneath it, and the bottom book overhangs the stand's front by 14 mm. The top book's spine is at x 39.0 [B: 38.4]; the pile's middle is at y 21.4 [B: 21.6]. From the top down the codes are MOTH, FERN, MINT, BRIM [B: DUSK, WREN, DUNE, LARK]. Shelf: fixed, wooden. A board 9.5 cm deep and 14.9 cm long whose top is 2.0 cm above the table, with a back wall and a left end wall 1.2 cm thick rising 7.0 cm above the board; the right end is open. The board's front edge is at x 42.0 [B: 41.4]; the left end's inside face is at y 13.6 [B: 13.8] and the board runs right from there to y -1.3 [B: -1.1]. The shelf is empty at the start. Both arms start in the raised ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: Tools: photos of the shelf from the front and from above, a ruler, a protractor or level app, and the trial video. Score = (number of books in place) / 4, read at the end of the run. A book is shelved when it stands on the shelf's board (its centre over the board, its bottom within 4 mm of the board's top), head up with its tail-to-head direction within 10 degrees of vertical, its spine facing the shelf's front within 20 degrees seen from above, still (moving slower than 5 cm/s) and let go (no gripper's grasp point within 2 cm of it). Read the shelved books from left to right as seen from the arms: a shelved book is in place when every shelved book to its left has an alphabetically earlier code and every shelved book to its right a later one. So 1.0 for four books in place, 0.75 for three, 0.5 for two, 0.25 for one, else 0. A book lying down, standing on its head, with its spine to the back, off the board or still in the pile is not shelved. The books need not touch each other.
reset_notes: Take the books off the shelf and rebuild the pile on the stand in the layout's order, face up, spines toward the arms, heads to the left, each book 14 mm nearer the arms than the one beneath.
fidelity: Books are rigid boxes (80 x 120 x 26 mm, 160 g); a real paperback flexes when held by one edge. The codes are block letters 21 mm tall drawn on the spine: at 320 x 176 they are easy to read in the wrist cameras at working distance and small in the top camera. The pile is staggered evenly, 14 mm per book, on a fixed stand, and the shelf is fixed. Grip force is not judged.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (a gripper went to the top of the pile several times but no book left it; the shelf stayed empty); demo: 1.0 (all four books standing in alphabetical order at step 1,134)
